items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: Then when Eddie called me three days later and he says, “We’d like to have you on the band,” I started to cry.

ctx.x: You didn’t know that you were talking to his wife.

Well of course I had remembered “Benny Rides Again” from 1939, which Eddie wrote for Benny Goodman. And then when I auditioned for the band, I didn’t believe it until I got to New York and saw who was there at the audition, that I was really auditioning for the Sauter-Finegan. Then when Eddie called me three days later and he says, “We’d like to have you on the band,” I started to cry.
And you left school to go do that?

items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: there and Al Block and Ray Sheiner

ctx.x: That was the road band. We spent weeks with auditions at Carol's studio and we got Harvey Estrom

there and Al Block and Ray Sheiner, Wally King--God bless Wally, Gene Allen; good players. Sonny Russo--we almost didn't get Sonny. Tommy Mitchell wanted to come as a B flat trombonist, wound up being one of the best bass trombonists in the country.
